title: Attachment guide
intro: What the attachments actually do, so you know why a build looks the way it does.

sections.title: How attachments work
sections.summary: Every gun has a 100-point budget. Each attachment costs points, so a build is a set of trade-offs.
points: Attachments unlock by levelling that gun (kills and damage with it), from level 0 up to about 40.
Dashed tags like S3 HW 6 come from seasonal Hardware challenges, not from weapon level.
Most strong builds spend points in this order: grip, muzzle, magazine, scope — then ammo or a laser with what is left.
Until you reach the level for a part, use any unlocked part in the same slot.

sections.title: Grips
sections.summary: The grip (underbarrel) decides how fast you aim and how much the gun kicks.

rows: speed and control, but up to 45 pts

sections.tip: Slim Angled vs Full Angled: same aim speed. Slim keeps you mobile and accurate while strafing; Full gives a little more recoil control. That is why fast close–mid builds use Slim.
points: Aim speed comes from grips,      some barrels and smaller magazines on some guns — never from lasers.

sections.title: Muzzles
sections.summary: Mostly about whether enemies can see you shoot. Brakes and compensators put you on the enemy minimap.

columns: Shows you on the enemy minimap

sections.tip: Default to a suppressor. Take a brake only if recoil is your real problem and you fight far away — or so close that you are seen anyway. Shotguns use the CQB Suppressor because it keeps hip-fire accurate.

sections.title: Lasers
sections.summary: Lasers never change aim speed. They improve hip-fire, and the blue and violet ones steady your aim while moving.
points: SMGs and close-range carbines (SG 553R, M4A1, Brod 3): 5 MW Green — or 5 MW Red if you flank and want no beam.
Assault rifles and mid-range carbines: 50 MW Violet, or no laser and spend the points on the grip or suppressor.
Skip 120 MW Blue — 30 points rarely fits the budget.
sections.tip: A laser is the last thing you buy, with leftover points.

sections.title: Ammo
sections.summary: Ammo changes headshot damage or adds a side effect. Body damage stays the same.

rows: spray or hip-fire guns — save the points
you tap heads at mid range

shoots through thin cover, a bit more recoil
your hits delay enemy health regeneration

sections.tip: Hollow Point only matters when it saves a shot. Example: on the B36A4 or M4A1 up close, two headshots plus one body shot do 98.8 damage with FMJ (no kill) but 104 with Hollow Point — a 3-shot kill instead of 4.
